messages.subject_clean: Save additional estimates in output (from a mediation model)
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the helpful workaround, Amanda.  Is there any progress on this?  It'd be great to be able to include indirect effects in the model output to be read by R.

-Isaac

On Wednesday, December 18, 2013 at 5:32:16 PM UTC-5, Amanda Gottschall wrote:
> Hi Cathy,
>
> I'm a user of the MplusAutomation package and have been able to obtain mediation estimates when reading the Mplus output file into R.  Rather than using the MODEL INDIRECT command in Mplus you can manually define all mediation effects of interest by labeling the relevant path estimates and then calculating the mediated effect in MODEL CONSTRAINT.  All new parameters defined in MODEL CONSTRAINT (e.g., your specific mediated effects) are read in with other parameter estimates using the extractModelParameters function (which is also a part of the ReadModels function) in the MplusAutomation package.  Here is a brief example of how you would specify your mediation model in Mplus so that you can extract the mediated effect using the MplusAutomation in R:
>
> MODEL:
>   m ON x (p1) ; ! mediation a path (parameter is labeled p1)
>   y ON x m (p2-p3) ; ! mediation c' and b paths (labeled p2 and p3, respectively)
> MODEL CONSTRAINT:
>   NEW (ab) ; ! create a new variable called 'ab'
>   ab = p1 * p3 ; ! 'ab' mediated effect = a path * b path
>
> I hope this helps everyone!
> Amanda
>
>
> On Tuesday, July 16, 2013 6:33:48 PM UTC-4, Cathy Antonakos wrote:
> > This is a great program! I am using Mplus to test indirect effects in many path models, and just used Mplus Automation for the first time this week!
> >
> > Is it possible to save the estimates from the total, direct, and indirect effects section of the output? I can obtain the parameter estimates from the OLS and probit regressions. But I'd especially like to obtain the estimates of the indirect effects.
> >
> > Thanks.
> > Cathy
